response:
Thought for 28s

1. 3 most important things missing from the brief format (beyond notes):

Open deals / pipeline status. Zero visibility into quotes out, active opportunities, or stalled deals. Sebastian walks in blind on follow-ups.
Last interaction summary + crystal-clear call objective. No “what happened last time” or “goal of THIS call = book site visit / close Q3 retreat.” V1 is a data dump, not a battle plan.
Tailored questions + triggers. No pre-loaded 3 questions based on industry news, expansions, or past pain. He’ll default to generic “how’s business?” bullshit.

2. Rules-based call prep hints: They create false confidence. Period.
Generic rules spit out the same amber-box fluff for any “VIP” with sauna tags. New rep reads it, feels prepped, then sounds like a robot on the call. They’re lazy crutches that ignore the 95% of cards with real notes. Kill them or make them note-driven only.

3. Physical kanban Week 1: Absolute shit idea. High-risk data loss from day 1.
New rep juggling top-20 revenue clients + Post-its = lost notes, forgotten updates, transcription errors into registry.xlsx. “Cute visibility” is owner fantasy. Force digital (Trello/Notion view of xlsx) immediately. Double data entry kills accuracy and momentum.

4. World-class B2B hotel/venue sales pre-call brief:
One-page, scannable in 2-3 minutes max (what Sebastian actually has time for).

Header: company + VIP badge + total_rev rank.
Contact block + LinkedIn/personal trigger.
Rich relationship history (pulled straight from customer_notes — key excerpts, preferences, past issues resolved).
Pipeline snapshot: open deals, quotes pending, last interaction.
Insights/red flags: recent company news, expansion triggers, buying process.
Personalised hooks + 3 tailored questions to ask.
Suggested call objective + next action.
Tailored upsell ideas based on favourite_services + typical_season.
Modern teams (top hospitality CRMs) auto-generate this from CRM + notes. No generic scoring line. No rules-based hints.

5. Single highest-leverage change that improves call quality the most:
Force customer_notes into every brief right now.
95% of cards have gold — relationship history, preferences, special requirements, past issues. Currently invisible. This single change turns Sebastian from “Hi, we do retreats” into “I saw your team loved the X event last summer and we fixed the AV issue — ready to lock in Q2?” Personalisation wins B2B venue sales. Everything else (hints, kanban, scoring) is noise until notes are front-and-center.

Do this before April 7 or you’re wasting the new rep’s first 30 days on amateur hour. Attack fixed. Owner, total_rev focus: implement notes + pipeline + objectives in V2 HTML briefs by April 6. No excuses.
